text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein to offer condolences to families for the Israeli victims on Sunday and will meet Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu in Israel.
- Prime Minister Abdul Karim al-Kabariti opens Saudi industrial exhibition.
- Parliamentary session to be dissolved on March 19. Opposition seeks emergency session.
- No tangible results to international meeting in Gaza. PLO leader Yasser Arafat calls on Israel to revise its settlement plans.
- Jordanian air force picks up 27 Jordanians who had fled Albania to Italy.
- King says investigation into the shooting by the Jordanian soldier of Israeli school girls will uncover the truth.
- Israel pollutes Jordan River with sewage.
- Royal decree dissolving the ordinary session of parliament.
- Egyptian embassy calls on Egyptian labourers in Jordan to rectify their residence status.
- Cabinet urges saving the Middle East peace process from extremism and Israeli creation of facts on the ground; and praises the "king for keeping Jordan's image pure."
- Elections to the council of Jordan University students union on Monday; 74 Islamic candidates are standing.
- Prime Minister Kabariti says Jordan seeks to end the trade protocol with Saudi Arabia and move towards free trade.
- Senate and cabinet "condemn criminal act" by Jordanian soldier.
- Switch to summer time on April 4.
